observations: Photo 0: shows a Nikon-branded box printed 'D750' and a separate 'Nikkor Lens 50' box, sitting on a couch; a printed image of a gimbal-mounted camera appears on a larger box behind them (looks like a stock/promotional image on a Zhiyun gimbal box, not a photo of the actual item).
Photo 1: shows the opened D750 box containing only printed manuals ('D750 User's Manual', French manual), no camera body visible.

No photo shows the actual camera body, lens glass, LCD screen, serial number, shutter count, or any functioning indicator.
No image confirms the camera power-on, lens mount, or physical body condition (scratches, dents, mold).

risks.proof: Photo of the actual camera body out of the box, showing the Nikon logo, lens mount, and LCD screen powered on.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified/no body confirmed, i.e. cannot be priced as a working D750

risks.risk: Shutter count and sensor condition unknown, critical for D750 pricing.
risks.proof: Photo of the info/shooting-data screen showing shutter actuation count.
risks.if_unproven: priced at worst case (high shutter count / heavy use)

risks.risk: Possible grey-market or non-functional unit misrepresented as 'American used'.
risks.proof: Photo of body serial number matching any warranty card or box sticker.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified origin, standard used-market price only

risks.risk: Lens (Nikkor 50mm) condition and whether it's included in sale or just shown for display.
risks.proof: Photo of the lens itself, front and rear elements, aperture blades.
risks.if_unproven: priced as body-only, lens excluded unless proven

proof_requests: Photo of the actual camera body outside the box, front and top view showing Nikon D750 nameplate and lens mount.
Photo of the LCD screen powered on, showing menu or shutter count.
Photo of the serial number on the body base plate.
Photo/video of the camera firing the shutter or taking a test shot.
Photo of the Nikkor 50mm lens itself (not just its box).
response.reason: All three photos show only packaging, manuals, and bubble wrap; no camera body, lens, or screen is actually visible, so condition and even the existence of the claimed D750 cannot be assessed or priced.
